EOMasters News

These two videos are again from the Mini but Might series. The first is about the four different resolutions we face when working with remote sensing data. The second focuses on the spatial resolution of radar data.

  • EOMMini Resolutions in Earth Observation - YouTube

  • Discuss in the EOMasters Forum  

New Blog: The Earth is in our Hands. Really?

Earth observation and remote sensing are key branches of science that employ satellite data to monitor and comprehend the Earth and its surroundings. However, many researchers and consumers find it difficult to get and use satellite imagery due to a variety of reasons such as cost, availability, quality, and complexity.
Let's have a look at the current status.

  • The Earth is in our Hands. Really?

  • EOMasters Newsletter Archive

EO and RS News

Farmers, Phones and Satellite Data

NASA reports on how farmers use their smartphones to collect field data and monitor their crop conditions using satellite data and mobile apps. GeoFairy allows them to assessing crop growth anomalies that indicate potential stress or damage and agricultural personnel use SERVIR’s Rice Map Engine application to combine field data from GeoFairy, satellite data, and crop trends to produce a final rice map. Finally, farmers are provided with timely and accurate information on their crop conditions and management options.

  • Phone to Food: Mapping Rice in Nepal | NASA Applied Sciences

Thousands of Sentinel-2 Products Must be Ignored

During the reprocessing for the Sentinel-2 Collection-1 a problem occurred and thousands of L1C and L2A products having anomalous TCI component metadata have been disseminated. A list of such products is provided, and everyone is advised not to download or to delete them if already done.

  • Copernicus Sentinel-2 Collection-1 - Few anomalous products to be ignored

  • List of affected products (Excel File)

Ocean Colour is Changing

A group of scientists have analysed 20 years of MODIS data from 2002 to 2022 and noticed that 56% of ocean surfaces have become greener. This might be a result of climate change, but the real cause is not yet known.

  • More Than Half the World’s Ocean Surface Is Getting Greener

  • Global climate-change trends detected in indicators of ocean ecology

Software and Tools

QGIS Server got OGC Certified

QGIS has announced that QGIS Server LTR 3.28 is now certified against WMS 1.3.0. Thes last years, they worked a lot towards a robust implementation of the WMS 1.3.0 specification.

  • QGIS server 3.28 is officially OGC compliant

Beyond EO

Men were Hunters and Women Gatherers

This is still the general idea when we think of prehistoric times. But a new study is challenging this stereotype and supports the idea that women had an important role in hunting activities. The atlatl, a spear thrower device, enabled more people to participate in hunting activities by reducing the advantage of male strength. The atlatl could have been a tool that led to gender equality.

  • Atlatl use equalizes female and male projectile weapon velocity

That's it for this issue. I hope you enjoyed this collection of news. Stay tuned for the next edition, which will arrive in your inbox in about two weeks.

Tschüss and Goodbye!

Marco
